text: The person receiving care should control the guide. What Helps Me is a private support passport inspired by NHS health and care passport guidance.
The owner starts with their own Remnic notes. They select only what helps, then give clear consent before any model sees the text.
Drafting uses the model route already configured in Remnic: a local model, an OpenClaw gateway, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or direct OpenAI. No separate OpenAI setup is required.
The model is the scribe. The person is the author. Every card stays a draft until the owner edits and approves it.
The owner shares only approved cards, for a limited time. The link pins the exact words they reviewed.
A helper opens a focused guide. They cannot see source notes, search memories, or browse anything else in Remnic.
Questions stay grounded in the shared guide. Each answer cites the exact card, so the helper can check the source.
Consent can change. The owner stops sharing once, and the next helper request locks the guide immediately.
The helper sees a clear locked state. The private notes never moved, and the owner remains in control.
What Helps Me gives support that travels, while control stays with the person.
